spec.title: ZAP: validating the NEXT import and data prototype

status.comment: 2026-09-12. Report on an isolated data experiment, not on running or implementing NEXT.

p.PILOT-SUBJECT: The input was the shared campaigns/next/plan.seed.toml revision 3 and 90 task-contract files at source commit 4febb04d02bd7853776895c38ea87a9783e05a0c. The import contained 425 nodes, 212 tasks, and 64 mandates. The complete plan values and every contract were compared with the source, including extensions, ordering, states, acceptance, and evidence. Source plan hash: 0eecdbae2aa15542f4ac17fe2a8b5986ef4637bac3e041ed899a04e71e78284c.

p.PILOT-ISOLATION: The experiment ran in a new user-local store separate from the active MUP context. All 91 source files were preserved byte for byte. The immutable base and the original 425 nodes and contracts remained unchanged after events were recorded. Three explicitly synthetic nodes were added to the copy to test structural lowering, for a total of 428; they are not newly approved campaign tasks. MUP, NEXT-EXECUTION-AUTHORITY, and all other constraints were unchanged.

p.PILOT-JOURNAL: The journal contains an import receipt and 12 events of eight supported kinds. Recalculation produces a byte-identical canonical JSON representation of state. Repeating a command with the same ID and content does not add an event. The decision rationale and its link to an observation are available from the data without a model. The source base remains unchanged.

p.PILOT-STOPS: The pilot verified clear when no condition holds, needs_evidence when migration impact is unknown, pause before changing a public format when the migration affects data, and too_late for the same assessment after the action. An infrastructure failure does not increment the architectural counter. An unavailable observation does not by itself complete an approach. One failure does not trigger; two distinct approaches to one synthetic problem produce pause after replay. The checks granted no authority to act.

p.PILOT-VERIFICATION: Eighteen focused unittest scenarios for the new kernel passed, as did checks of two SKILL.md files and a package-only vibe check: 0 errors and 0 warnings. The full product panel, Rust build, and mutation testing were not run. The machine-readable pilot-report.json records the kernel hash, base, counts, and separately verified properties.

p.PILOT-LIMITS: The pilot remains draft, owner_contract is absent, the frontier is empty, and dispatch is not authorized. Failure observations in the example are synthetic and are not VibeVM defects. The pilot demonstrates preservation and structural validation of data, not the semantic sufficiency of the new decomposition or the truth of any arbitrary fact. At the time of this pilot on 2026-09-12, trusted owner control, automatic reassessment of native facts, the runner, server stream, and Qwik viewer had not yet been implemented; this is a dated historical boundary of the pilot, not a list of current package capabilities.

p.PILOT-REPRODUCTION: The shared input can be imported again with zap_state.py import-mup --plan campaigns/next/plan.seed.toml --tasks-dir campaigns/next/tasks --out NEW_LOCAL_DIRECTORY, then inspected with inspect and events. Paths are relative to the selected host checkout; the package itself stores only a small report, not a copy of the personal plan. The 18 independent fixture scenarios can be reproduced from the package root with python -B -m unittest discover -s vibevm/vibespecs/skills/zap-state/scripts -p test_zap_state.py. The local base contains captured absolute paths and the import-receipt UUID, so its hash attests to that specific capture rather than promising identical bytes on another machine.
